title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). V is a complete DVR with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, fraction field K and S = Spec V. M = (M(n)) is a p-Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) group over K. M satisfies the 'monodromy condition' if it has a composition series whose graded pieces acquire good reduction after a finite separable extension. Choose K'/K finite Galois with group G that works for all the pieces (a 'field of virtual good reduction'), and let S' be the normalisation of S in K'. By Tate's full faithfulness theorem (then known only when K has characteristic 0), each piece extends uniquely to a BT group over S' carrying a G-action semilinear over S'. K_BT(K;K') is the Grothendieck group of BT groups over K having K' as field of virtual good reduction. Map (1) goes K_BT(K;K') → K_BT(S',G).

This page.
(2) S' is local with closed point s'. Restricting to the special fibre gives K_BT(S',G) → K_BT(s',G); G acts on s', not necessarily faithfully.
(3) k' = k(s') is perfect. So the covariant Dieudonné functor BT(s') → Modlib(W(k')) is available. The handwritten note says it is an equivalence onto crystals, i.e. Dieudonné modules with F and V. G acts on k' and hence on W(k'), so the functor gives semilinear G-modules, and K_BT(s',G) → K(W(k'),G).
(4) Composing gives K_BT(K;K') → K(W(k'),G).

If k is algebraically closed, G = I acts trivially on k' and K(W(k'),G) = R_{W(k')}(G). In general, restrict to the inertia subgroup I ⊂ G, which acts W(k')-linearly. This gives K(W(k'),G) → K(W(k'),I)^G ≃ R_{W(k')}(I)^{G/I}. Here G acts on R(I) by conjugation on I together with transport of structure on W(k'); inner automorphisms act trivially, so G-invariants equal G/I-invariants.
(5) Taking traces gives K_BT(K,K') → R_{W(k')}(I)^G → Cent(I,W(k'))^G.

The image of cl(M) is called the character of M: a W(k')-valued class function φ_M on inertia, G-equivariant in the sense φ(gig⁻¹) = g(φ(i)). It is independent of K' and so can be viewed as a function on the (infinite) inertia subgroup of Gal(K̄/K).

Modern reading: φ_M is the trace of inertia acting on the Dieudonné module, i.e. on D_cris(V_p M|_{K'}). Equivalently it is the character of the inertial restriction of the Weil–Deligne representation (the 'inertial type') of a potentially Barsotti–Tate representation, with N = 0.

The page ends by starting the case where M_{K'} is constant (étale). The next page shows that φ_M then equals the Brauer character of _pM on p'-elements of I. It asks whether this holds in general, i.e. whether the type on p'-inertia is determined by the mod-p representation. It disproves this with M = Z_p(1) when μ_p ⊄ K. It then poses a test question: two elliptic curves with potentially good reduction, isomorphic p-torsion and μ_p ⊂ K — do their inertia traces on p'-elements agree? The interesting case is supersingular reduction.

Purpose: to define an inertia-type invariant for potentially good BT groups using only p-adic, crystalline data, as a p-adic analogue of the ℓ-adic inertia characters of SGA 7 IX. The text itself notes these can be computed via T_ℓ for any prime ℓ.
errors: Typo 'intertie' for 'inertie'; inconsistent notation K_BT(K;K') vs K_BT(K,K').

The definition of K_BT(K;K') and of map (1) silently needs exactness of 'extension to S'' on short exact sequences. This is true: the schematic closure of a BT subgroup is a BT group (Tate) plus full faithfulness. It is not argued here.
Everything rests on Tate's theorem, so the construction is only justified when char K = 0 at this date. The equal-characteristic case is due to de Jong (1998).
The claim of independence from K' is asserted as 'easy' without proof; it is plausible, via compatibility of Dieudonné modules with base change W(k') → W(k'').
No real mathematical error; the W(k')-valued character has a semilinear G-equivariance whose descent to W(k) or Z_p is not discussed (the margin of the next page speculates about it).

ideas.what: Using Tate's full faithfulness to give the good-reduction model over S' a semilinear Galois action (descent data), for a BT group with potentially good reduction
ideas.modern_name: potentially Barsotti–Tate groups / descent data on p-divisible groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1967); systematic use by Conrad–Diamond–Taylor, Breuil, Kisin
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in Grothendieck's ICM 1970 talk 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux' / Montréal 1970 notes; unsure

ideas.what: Character of a potentially good BT group: trace of inertia acting (W(k')-linearly) on the Dieudonné module of the reduction over K', as a W(k')-valued class function on inertia independent of K'
ideas.modern_name: inertial type of a potentially Barsotti–Tate / potentially crystalline representation (inertial part of Fontaine's Weil–Deligne representation from D_pcris)

ideas.where_published: not known to appear in published Grothendieck texts

ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical via endomorphisms of the reduction; general potentially semistable case Ochiai (1999), Fontaine's conjectures, Coleman–Iovita

missed.claim: In 1969 Grothendieck already attaches to a potentially good BT group the inertia character on its crystalline (Dieudonné) realisation over the field of good reduction. This is exactly the 'inertial type' of a potentially Barsotti–Tate representation, which later became central in Conrad–Diamond–Taylor and Breuil–Mézard. On the next page he asks how this type relates to the mod-p representation _pM on p'-inertia. That is the type-versus-reduction question underlying Breuil–Mézard multiplicities and Serre-weight problems.
missed.quote: l'image de cl(M) dans le dernier membre est appelé le caractère du groupe de B.T. M ... la fonction caractère est alors envisagée comme fonction sur le sous-groupe d'inertie (infini) de Gal(K̄/K)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precursor, uncredited in the literature, of inertial types and of Fontaine's Weil–Deligne representation for potentially crystalline representations. It also shows Grothendieck considering early the compatibility of p-adic types with mod-p reductions.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete question about whether the tame inertial type is determined by the residual representation. Partial answers exist implicitly in the theory of types and Serre weights, but it is not posed this way in the literature I know.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean 1969 definition of what is essentially the inertial type of a potentially Barsotti–Tate representation, via crystalline realisation. It is linked to a question about its relation to the mod-p representation, prefiguring 1990s–2000s work by Fontaine, CDT and Breuil–Mézard. It is a natural construction once Tate's theorem and Dieudonné theory are available, so only moderately surprising.
